result.answer: Salience: frequency of mention, positioning/paragraph position, grammatical function/internal POS structure, and relative entity frequency (paragraph coverage plus exponential decay by paragraph index). Relative authority: comparison of an entity’s a priori authority—corpus occurrence probability or PageRank centrality over an entity–news graph—against co-occurring entities, measured as the proportion of co-occurring entities with higher a priori authority (with optional threshold relaxation). [S:b9011f5a9270#28] [S:b9011f5a9270#45] [S:b9011f5a9270#46] [S:b9011f5a9270#51] [S:b9011f5a9270#54]

claims.text: Frequent salience features include entity frequency in a document, entity positioning, grammatical function, and internal entity structure such as POS tags and head nouns.
claims.note: Span explicitly lists frequency, positioning, grammatical function, and internal structure like POS tags/head nouns.

claims.text: The paper reimplements Dunietz and Gillick salience features, including positional features, occurrence frequency, and the internal POS structure of the entity and its sentence.
claims.note: Span states reimplementation of Dunietz and Gillick features including positional, frequency, and internal POS structure of entity and sentence.

claims.text: Relative entity frequency rewards entities that occur throughout the text, measured by the number of paragraphs, and rewards entities in opening paragraphs via exponential decay by paragraph index.
claims.note: Span describes rewards for occurring throughout text by paragraph count and exponential decay by opening paragraph index.

claims.text: A priori entity authority is measured by the probability of the entity occurring in the corpus or by centrality measures such as PageRank on an entity–news graph.
claims.note: Span gives corpus probability and PageRank-style centrality on an entity/news article graph as approaches.

claims.text: Relative authority compares an entity's authority, such as frequency of mention, with the authority of its co-occurring entities.
claims.note: Span states relative authority compares an entity's authority, such as frequency of mention, with co-occurring entities' authority.

claims.text: Relative authority is defined as the proportion of co-occurring entities with a higher a priori authority than the entity.
claims.note: Span defines relative authority as proportion of co-occurring entities with higher a priori authority.

claims.text: Relative entity frequency models salience as an exponentially decaying function based on the paragraph position where the entity appears.
claims.note: Span says relative entity frequency models salience as exponential decay based on paragraph positional index.

claims.text: The model adds entity authority, news authority, and novelty features that measure relations between several entities, between entity and news article, and between competing news articles.
claims.note: Span states added entity authority, news authority, and novelty features measuring relations among entities, entity-article, and competing articles.

[s1-p5] Entity Salience. Determining which entities are prominent or salient in a given text has a long
history in NLP, sparked by the linguistic theory of Centering BIBREF14 . Salience has been used in
pronoun and co-reference resolution BIBREF15 , or to predict which entities will be included in an
abstract of an article BIBREF11 . Frequent features to measure salience include the frequency of an
entity in a document, positioning of an entity, grammatical function or internal entity structure (POS tags,
head nouns etc.). These approaches are not currently aimed at knowledge base generation or Wikipedia
coverage extension but we postulate that an entity's salience in a news article is a prerequisite to the
news article being relevant enough to be included in an entity page. We therefore use the salience
features in BIBREF11 as part of our model. However, these features are document-inte

citations.title: qasper-fb1227b3681c69f60eb0539e16c5a8cd784177a7 - 1703.10344.md
citations.text:
[s5-p5] Baseline Features. As discussed in Section SECREF2 , a variety of features that measure
salience of an entity in text are available from the NLP community. We reimplemented the ones in
Dunietz and Gillick BIBREF11 . This includes a variety of features, e.g. positional features, occurrence
frequency and the internal POS structure of the entity and the sentence it occurs in. Table 2 in BIBREF11
gives details.

[s5-p29] In Figure FIGREF60 we show the impact of the individual feature groups that contribute to the
superior performance in comparison to the baselines. Relative entity frequency from the salience feature,
models the entity salience as an exponentially decaying function based on the positional index of the
paragraph where the entity appears. The performance of INLINEFORM0 with relative entity frequency
from the salience feature group is close to that of all the features combined. The authority and novelty
features account to a further improvement in terms of precision, by adding roughly a 7%-10% increase.
